title: WPSS/1719/2026 of SHAMSHER SINGH Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
UKHC010116132026
2026:UHC:5566
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition Service Single No. 1719 of 2026
08 July, 2026
Shamsher Singh
--Petitioner
Versus
State Of Uttarakhand and others
--Respondents
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Presence:-
Mr. Tarun Prakash Singh Takuli, Advocate for the Applicant.
Mr. N.S. Pundir, learned Dy.A.G. for the State.
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Hon'ble Pankaj Purohit, J. (Oral)
By means of this writ petition, petitioner has
sought quashing of order dated 30.06.2026 passed by
respondent no.2 to the extent whereby petitioner, who is
working as Senior Administrative Officer, has been
transferred from Training and Employment Directorate,
Uttarakhand, Haldwani (Nainital) to Government
Industrial Training Institute, Pithoragarh.
2. Facts of the case are that the petitioner was
initially appointed as a Junior Assistant in the year 2006
in the Training & Employment Directorate, Uttarakhand,
Haldwani. During the course of his service, he was
promoted to the posts of Senior Assistant, Head Assistant
and thereafter Administrative Officer, on which post he
was posted at Government Industrial Training Institute,
Pithoragarh. Subsequently, on his promotion to the post
of Senior Administrative Officer, he was transferred and
posted at the Training & Employment Directorate,
Uttarakhand, Haldwani, where he joined pursuant to the
order dated 09.10.2024. The wife of the petitioner is
stated to be suffering from 100% permanent disability
(hearing and speech impairment).
1

UKHC010116132026
2026:UHC:5566
3. It is stated that while the department was
preparing the eligibility list of annual transfers for the
year 2026-27, the petitioner submitted the disability
certificate of his wife before respondent no.2 on
26.05.2026. Thereafter, respondent no. 2 issued the
transfer order dated 30.06.2026 transferring the
petitioner from the Training & Employment Directorate,
Uttarakhand, Haldwani to Government Industrial
Training Institute, Pithoragarh. The transfer list was
thereafter published on 03.07.2026. The petitioner has
also placed on record the eligibility list prepared for the
annual transfer exercise and claims that out of eight
Senior Administrative Officers shown as eligible for
transfer, only two officers, including the petitioner, were
transferred from an accessible area to a remote area.
Aggrieved by the transfer order dated 30.06.2026,
petitioner has filed the present writ petition seeking its
quashing to the extent it relates to him.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that
the impugned transfer order dated 30.06.2026 is
arbitrary, illegal and has been issued in complete
disregard of the provisions of the Uttarakhand Annual
Transfer for Public Servants Act, 2017. It is submitted
that the petitioner's wife is suffering from 100%
permanent hearing and speech disability and the
disability certificate was duly submitted before the
competent authority on 26.05.2026 during the annual
transfer exercise. However, the respondents failed to
consider the said certificate and proceeded to transfer the
petitioner from Haldwani to Pithoragarh. It is contended
that in view of Sections 3(e), 7(d)(iii) and 13(4) of the Act,
petitioner was entitled to exemption from transfer, and,
2

UKHC010116132026
2026:UHC:5566
in absence of any exceptional administrative exigency or
reasons recorded by the competent authority, impugned
transfer order is liable to be quashed.
5. Learned counsel further submits that the
transfer exercise has been carried out in a discriminatory
and arbitrary manner. Referring to the eligibility list, it is
argued that although several Senior Administrative
Officers were eligible for transfer, only two officers,
including the petitioner, were transferred from accessible
areas to remote areas, while other similarly situated
employees were either retained at their existing places of
posting or granted exemption on account of disability. It
is contended that the respondents have selectively
applied the provisions of the Transfer Act without any
rational basis, thereby violating the mandate of Article 14
of the Constitution of India. It is further submitted that
the petitioner had not even completed two years at his
present place of posting when the impugned order came
to be issued.
6. Learned counsel submits that the respondents
acted mechanically without considering the petitioner's
representation and the disability certificate submitted by
him, rendering the impugned order arbitrary and
unsustainable in law. It is further argued that the
transfer order has been issued with mala fide intent to
victimize the petitioner, who intended to contest the
election of the ministerial employees' association. On
these grounds, it is prayed that the writ petition be
allowed and the impugned transfer order dated
30.06.2026, to the extent it relates to the petitioner, be
quashed.
3

UKHC010116132026
2026:UHC:5566
7. Having heard the learned Counsel for the
parties and after perusal of the material available on
record, this Court is of the considered opinion that no
case for interference with the impugned transfer order is
made out. It is a settled proposition of law that transfer is
an incidence of service and an employee holding a
transferable post has no vested right to remain posted at
a particular place. The scope of judicial review in matters
relating to transfer is extremely limited and this Court
would ordinarily not interfere with a transfer order unless
the same is shown to be in violation of any statutory
provision, passed by an incompetent authority or vitiated
by mala fides or patent arbitrariness.
8. The principal contention of the petitioner is
that his wife is suffering from 100% permanent disability
and, therefore, he was entitled to exemption from transfer
under the provisions of the Uttarakhand Annual Transfer
for Public Servants Act, 2017. However, merely because
the spouse of the petitioner is suffering from disability
would not confer upon the petitioner an absolute or
indefeasible right to remain posted at a particular
station. From the eligibility list, it is quite apparent that
the petitioner has served in accessible area for 7216 days
i.e. a period of around 20 years.
9. The petitioner has failed to demonstrate that
the impugned transfer order has been passed in
contravention of any mandatory statutory provision so as
to warrant interference by this Court in exercise of its
writ jurisdiction. Furthermore, the plea of discrimination
raised by the petitioner is also devoid of substance.
Merely because some other employees have not been
transferred or have allegedly been granted exemption
4

UKHC010116132026
2026:UHC:5566
would not, by itself, render the transfer of the petitioner
illegal. It is well settled that transfer is primarily an
administrative matter and unless hostile discrimination
or arbitrariness is established by cogent material, no
interference is called for. Likewise, the allegations of mala
fides are vague and bald in nature. No specific officer
against whom mala fides have been alleged has been
impleaded by name, nor has any material been placed on
record to substantiate such allegations.
10. In view of the aforesaid discussion, this Court
finds no illegality, arbitrariness or mala fides in the
impugned transfer order warranting interference under
Article 226 of the Constitution of India.
11. Accordingly, the writ petition, being devoid of
merit, is dismissed.
12. Pending application, if any, stands disposed of.
 (Pankaj Purohit, J.)
 08.07.2026
R.Dang
